explanation: The Andes are still rising as the Pacific sea floor slides beneath South America, which is why the range has so many volcanoes and earthquakes.

claims.text: The Andes run along the western side of South America.
The Sierra Madre ranges are in Mexico, and the Brazilian and Guiana Highlands lie in eastern and northern South America.
The Andes are being pushed up as oceanic plates of the Pacific slide beneath South America.
Subduction makes volcanoes and earthquakes common along the Andes.

evidence.restatement: The Andes run the length of South America's western side, from Venezuela and Colombia to Patagonia.
The Sierra Madre ranges are in Mexico; the Brazilian Highlands are in eastern Brazil and the Guiana Highlands in northern South America.
The Andes are pushed up as the Nazca and Antarctic plates subduct beneath South America.
That subduction makes volcanoes and earthquakes common along the Andes.
